# Concave remainder roots and local fraction capture do not imply a cap cover

For every integer `d>=2` there is an actual convex body with three positive
integer fibers and three closed ambient caps such that:

* every integer fiber has at least one cap capturing exactly its
  Grünbaum fraction `gamma_d`;
* all three strict-uncaptured d-volume roots are concave even on the
  entire real base interval;
* every cap has mass strictly below `gamma_d M/2`;
* the caps do not cover the mixed source.

Thus an actual cap cover cannot be replaced by either per-fiber fractional
capture or concavity of all scalar remainder profiles. This is not an OC
counterexample.

## 1. Actual body and exact caps

Put

    gamma=(d/(d+1))^d,  a=1-gamma,  c=a^(1/d),
    T={x in R^d: x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},  v=|T|=1/d!.

Here `0<c<1` and `gamma<1/2`. For the latter, the binomial expansion gives
`(1+1/d)^d>=2+(d-1)/(2d)>2` when `d>=2`.

In `R x R^d`, define

    C=conv(({−1} x cT) union ({0} x T) union ({1} x cT)).

This is a compact full-dimensional convex body. Its real fiber at
`z in [-1,1]` is exactly

    C_z=r(z)T,   r(z)=1-(1-c)|z|.                      (1)

Indeed `r` is concave, the set in (1) is equivalently given by
`x_i>=0` and `sum x_i+(1-c)|z|<=1`, and its two linear pieces are precisely
the convex hulls of the displayed endpoint and middle fibers. Its only
integer fibers are `cT,T,cT`, of volumes `av,v,av`; hence

    M=(1+2a)v=(3-2gamma)v.                            (2)

Write `s(x)=sum_i x_i` and use the closed caps

    H_0={s(x)>=c},
    H_-={s(x)>=1+(1-c^2)z},
    H_+={s(x)>=1-(1-c^2)z}.                           (3)

For `0<=h<=R`, the simplex slice `{x in RT:s(x)<h}` has volume `h^d v`.
Changing `<` to `<=` changes no d-volume, since its boundary is a proper
hyperplane. Thus every strict-complement computation below agrees with
closed cap mass exactly.

The cap `H_0` has zero endpoint mass and middle mass
`(1-c^d)v=gamma v`. For `H_-`, its thresholds at `z=-1,0,1` are
`c^2,1,2-c^2`. The first satisfies `0<c^2<c`; the last exceeds `c` because

    2-c^2-c=(1-c)(2+c)>0.

Its middle cap is only a facet, with zero d-volume, and its right cap is
empty. Its sole positive contribution is therefore

    |cT|-|c^2T|=(c^d-c^(2d))v
                =(a-a^2)v=gamma a v.                 (4)

Reflection in `z` proves the same statement for `H_+` on the right.
Consequently the maximum cap mass is exactly

    B=gamma v < gamma(3-2gamma)v/2 = gamma M/2,        (5)

where strictness is equivalent to `gamma<1/2`.

At the middle fiber `H_0` captures fraction gamma. At the left fiber
`H_-` captures fraction `gamma a v/(av)=gamma`; at the right fiber `H_+`
does the same. This proves the asserted local fractional capture.

## 2. Exact concave strict-remainder profiles

Let `e_i(z)=|C_z minus (H_i)_z|`. After dividing the volume roots by
`v^(1/d)`, the profiles on the entire interval `[-1,1]` are

    e_0(z)^(1/d)/v^(1/d)=c,

    e_-(z)^(1/d)/v^(1/d)=1+(1-c^2)z,   -1<=z<=0;
                          1-(1-c)z,      0<=z<=1,

    e_+(z)=e_-(-z).                                    (6)

For `H_0`, (1) always has radius at least c, so the strict remainder
is cT up to its null boundary. For `H_-` on the negative side, its
threshold is at most `r(z)`, since
`[(1-c^2)-(1-c)]z=c(1-c)z<=0`. On the positive side its threshold is
at least one, while `r(z)<=1`. This proves (6) directly from the simplex
slice formula. The left and right slopes of the second root profile are
`1-c^2` and `-(1-c)`, respectively, so it is concave. Reflection gives the
third profile; the first is constant. Their sampled triples are exactly

    (c,c,c),    (c^2,1,c),    (c,1,c^2).               (7)

No unsupported sampled-logconcavity assumption enters the example.

## 3. Missing coverage and the coefficient correction

Every point `(z,0)` with `-1<=z<=1` misses all three caps: every threshold
in (3) is strictly positive, its minimum being `c^2`. In particular the
actual mixed source has three explicitly uncovered points. Scalar local
fractional capture therefore cannot supply the missing geometric cover.

A tempting coefficient `gamma` in place of `1-c^2` in (3) works exactly
as claimed only when `d=2`. For general d, it gives left threshold
`1-gamma=c^d`, left strict-remainder root `c^d`, and captured volume

    [a-a^d]v,

rather than `gamma a v`. For example at `d=4`, `gamma=256/625` and
`a=369/625`, this erroneous cap has mass greater than `gamma v`.
The coefficient `1-c^2` is the exact all-dimensional correction, and
all assertions above use it.
